topic: Linear equations in one variable --- one, no, or infinitely many solutions
subtitle: One solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions

problems.slot: both sides simplify to (infinitely many solutions)
both sides simplify to (infinitely many solutions)

problems.desc: Part (b): explanation that once both sides are simplified the poster equation reads 8x + 20 = 8x + k, so subtracting 8x leaves 20 = k. Full credit requires the student to say that the variable terms cancel, leaving a statement about constants only, so any k other than 20 leaves a false numeric statement and therefore no solution. Accept wording such as 'the x terms disappear, so the equation is just 20 = k, which is false unless k is 20'. Do not accept a restatement of the answer k = 20 with no reference to the variable terms cancelling.

Part (b): explanation of what the simplified tank equation says about the two water amounts. Full credit requires the student to note that both tanks change by the same 9 litres per minute, so the difference between them stays fixed at 24 litres and the amounts are never equal. Accept a graph-based answer that says the two lines have the same rate of change and different starting amounts, so they are parallel and never meet. Do not accept 'no solution' alone with no reason.
